summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for observation following a transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure targeting a residual liver tumor in segment II. He had previously undergone radiofrequency ablation, which was complicated by a hemothorax. This admission was marked by post-procedural nausea and a low-grade fever, for which he received IV anti-emetics and a course of ciprofloxacin. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth. He developed a new headache, prompting a head CT that ruled out intracranial hemorrhage. His thrombocytopenia remained stable without bleeding. He improved clinically, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home on oral medications with instructions to complete antibiotics, manage nausea and pain as needed, and follow up as an outpatient.
